## freshRetries

| Key | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `freshRetries` | boolean | unset | a retry or fix build starts a fresh run (Tester notes + work so far in the prompt) instead of resuming the old, large session. |

## recoverOutput

| Key | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `recoverOutput` | boolean | unset | a builder whose output cannot be read is recovered from its session transcript instead of counting as a wasted build. |

## deployOnFailure

| Key | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `deployOnFailure` | `notify` \| `ticket` \| `fix` | unset | what a failed deploy does. notify (default) = the Retry card only; ticket = also a top-priority fix ticket; fix = that ticket is built at once (`dobby run <id>`), one message, and the fix's merge deploys again. One open fix per project. |

## deployFrom

| Key | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `deployFrom` | `checkout` \| `worktree` | unset | checkout (default) = the project's deploy_dir, pulled; worktree = a fresh worktree of origin/<base> from the project's repo for each deploy (its .env* files copied in), removed afterwards, so no separate release checkout is needed. |

## mergeChecks

| Key | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `mergeChecks` | `all` \| `required` | unset | which PR checks gate a merge. required (default) = the repo's required checks only (every check but Dobby's review when it requires none); all = every check. DOBBY_CHECKS=all\|required overrides. |

## reviewCap

| Key | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `reviewCap` | number (1–100) | unset | the 5-hour % review-scan may use, when looser than the builders' pace cap (reviews unblock merges). Unset = the builders' cap, as before. The week stays under pacing.weekCap either way. |

## billing

billing: plan (default) = a Claude Pro/Max sign-in, paced by its 5-hour and weekly windows. apiKey = no plan: every run, builders included, pays by the token through DOBBY_API_KEY, capped at dailyUsd per 24 hours and weeklyUsd per 7 days (the plan limits pacing.weekCap and the 5-hour pace do not apply; over the cap, `dobby limits` says Paused). workspaceId: the Console workspace id (wrkspc_...), for an organisation-level key not scoped to a workspace; sent as the anthropic-workspace-id header. Not a secret.

| Key | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `billing.mode` | `plan` \| `apiKey` | unset |  |
| `billing.dailyUsd` | number > 0 | `20` |  |
| `billing.weeklyUsd` | number > 0 | unset |  |
| `billing.workspaceId` | string | unset |  |
| `billing.planUsd` | number > 0 | unset |  |

## costComment

| Key | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `costComment` | boolean | unset | false = no cost comment on Dobby PRs (default on). billing.planUsd = what the owner pays for the plan; only the receipt card reads it. |

## safety

Safety (README "Safety"). preset: strict (every sensitive category waits for the owner) | balanced | autonomous. rules: per-category override of the preset: auto (normal review, then merge) | review (strict Opus review) | owner (needs-you card, no fix, no merge) | never (agents do not touch it). classifier: model (default) | jev | none. jev = the TypeSafe classifier (@typesafe-ai/sdk), optional: needs JEV_API_KEY in the environment, else the model is used. none = words only. unsure: what a classifier that cannot decide means: ask (send the owner a card) | allow (go on, at most a strict review).

| Key | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `safety.preset` | `strict` \| `balanced` \| `autonomous` | `balanced` |  |
| `safety.rules` | map of `migrations.schema` \| `migrations.data` \| `payments` \| `auth` \| `secrets` \| `deploys` \| `config` \| `client-sites` \| `releases` to `auto` \| `review` \| `owner` \| `never` | `{}` |  |
| `safety.classifier` | `jev` \| `model` \| `none` | `model` |  |
| `safety.unsure` | `ask` \| `allow` | `ask` |  |
| `safety.everyMerge` | `auto` \| `review` \| `owner` | unset | everyMerge: the floor for every merge, including changes in no category: auto \| review (strict review) \| owner (draft PR, the owner merges). Unset = the preset's (strict: owner, else auto). deploy: after a merge, ask (a Deploy tap; also when unset) \| auto (deploy at once, only when you set it). |
| `safety.deploy` | `auto` \| `ask` | unset |  |

## migrated

What `dobby migrate` found in the setup it migrated (a record; nothing reads it). Secret key NAMES only. launchdJobs is the file names of the com.dobby.* and com.foreman.* launch agents that were in ~/Library/LaunchAgents when it ran; Dobby does not install, remove or read them from here (`dobby jobs` does that).

| Key | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `migrated.at` | string | unset |  |
| `migrated.projects` | list of string | unset |  |
| `migrated.secretKeys` | list of string | unset |  |
| `migrated.discord` | map of string to string | unset |  |
| `migrated.launchdJobs` | list of string | unset |  |

<!-- manual/glossary.md -->
# Glossary

> The Dobby words you meet in the dashboard, the terminal and these docs, each with a link to the page that explains it.

The dashboard shows the same text behind its info icons.

## 5-hour window

Your plan also has a 5-hour limit. Dobby spreads the week across these windows so one busy window does not use up the week. [More](pacing.md#the-5-hour-window)

## Backlog

Tickets that are written but not queued. Nothing is built until you or the Engineering Manager queues one. [More](how-it-works.md#tickets)

## Billing

Plan mode runs on the part of your Claude plan you do not use. API key mode spends dollars, with a daily cap. [More](billing.md#which-one)

## Builder

The role that writes the code for a ticket, on its own branch, inside the sandbox. [More](roles.md#builder)

## Chief of Staff

The role that sends you a short brief every morning and evening. [More](roles.md#chief-of-staff)

## Classifier

What decides which safety category a change belongs to, such as payments or auth. The model is the default. [More](safety-categories.md#categories)

## Code Reviewer

The role that reviews every pull request Dobby opens and posts its findings on GitHub. [More](roles.md#code-reviewer)

## Done when

The line the Tester checks the finished work against. [More](how-it-works.md#tickets)

## Engineering Manager

The role that plans the work. It moves tickets from the backlog to the queue and writes new ones. [More](roles.md#engineering-manager)

## Goals

The larger outcomes your tickets belong to. They come from GitHub milestones or the Goals list in a project's dobby.md. [More](how-it-works.md#goals)

## Ideas

Suggestions from the Product Manager, the Engineering Manager and the Talent Scout. Turn one into a ticket or dismiss it. [More](roles.md#product-manager)

## Merging

The minimum every merge must meet: merge on its own, a strict review first, or you merge it yourself. [More](what-waits.md#the-floor-for-every-merge)

## Needs you

Things Dobby will not do alone: a merge you asked to approve, a deploy, or a question from a builder. [More](what-waits.md#needs-you)

## Paused

Stopped on purpose. A pause can cover everything, one part, one project or one ticket, and ends when you resume it. [More](pause-and-resume.md#pause-one-part)

## Product Manager

The role that ranks problems against your goals and writes idea cards and specs for large tickets. [More](roles.md#product-manager)

## Queue

Tickets marked ready, in the order builders will take them. Reorder it to change what gets built first. [More](how-it-works.md#tickets)

## Ready

Queued and waiting for a free builder. [More](how-it-works.md#tickets)

## Review cap

How much of the 5-hour window reviews may use. It can be higher than the builders' share, because reviews unblock merges. [More](config.md#reviewcap)

## Safety preset

How much Dobby may merge without you. Balanced, Strict or Autonomous. You can override single categories. [More](what-waits.md#safety-presets)

## Size

S, M or L, a rough measure of how big a ticket is. It sets how much of your week Dobby expects the ticket to use. [More](write-a-ticket.md#pick-a-size)

## Stop at

The share of your weekly plan Dobby may use. The rest of the week is yours. [More](pacing.md#the-weekly-cap)

## Supporting role

A smaller role that runs only when a ticket or a command needs it. [More](roles.md#supporting-roles)

## Talent Scout

A daily run that picks one role, looks for better skills for it and reviews the last 24 hours. Any change it makes arrives as a pull request. [More](roles.md#talent-scout)

## Tester

The role that checks a finished build against the ticket's done-when line. It can read files but not change them. [More](roles.md#tester)

## Ticket

A unit of work with a project, a title, a done-when line, a size and a priority. Everything Dobby builds starts as one. [More](how-it-works.md#tickets)

<!-- manual/safety-categories.md -->
# Safety categories

> The nine safety categories, the action each preset gives them, and what always waits for you.

The preset is `safety.preset` in your config. `safety.rules` overrides single categories, and `safety.everyMerge` sets the floor for every merge. [What waits for you](what-waits.md) explains how they fit together. To see how one ticket would be treated:

```sh
dobby safety explain "Add Stripe refunds to the orders page"
```

## Actions

| Action | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| `auto` | Normal review, then merge. |
| `review` | A strict review on the strongest model, then merge. |
| `owner` | Dobby opens a draft pull request and reviews it, and you merge it with `dobby merge <id>` or the Merge button on the dashboard. |
| `never` | Agents do not take the ticket. |

## Presets

| Category | Strict | Balanced | Autonomous |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `migrations.schema` | `owner` | `auto` | `auto` |
| `migrations.data` | `owner` | `owner` | `review` |
| `payments` | `owner` | `review` | `review` |
| `auth` | `owner` | `review` | `review` |
| `secrets` | `owner` | `review` | `review` |
| `deploys` | `owner` | `auto` | `auto` |
| `config` | `owner` | `auto` | `auto` |
| `client-sites` | `owner` | `owner` | `review` |
| `releases` | `owner` | `owner` | `review` |
| Every other merge | `owner` | `auto` | `auto` |

The last row is the floor that `safety.everyMerge` replaces. A change in several categories gets the strictest action among them.

## Categories

| Category | Covers |
| --- | --- |
| `migrations.schema` | A migration file that only changes the shape of the database, such as a new table, column or index. |
| `migrations.data` | A migration file that changes existing data: it updates, inserts or deletes rows, drops or renames a table or column, or changes a column type. A migration whose SQL Dobby cannot read counts here too. |
| `payments` | Code that handles real money: charging, billing, refunds, payouts, subscriptions or a payment provider. |
| `auth` | How people sign in: sessions, passwords, tokens, permissions or access control. |
| `secrets` | Secrets, tokens, API keys, passwords or credentials, or a change to a `.env` or `secrets` file. |
| `deploys` | Deploys and CI: a ticket about a deploy, production or a pipeline, or a change to `wrangler.toml`, `.github/workflows/` or a Dockerfile. |
| `config` | Config files such as `wrangler.toml`, `eas.json`, `app.json` or `*.config.*`, or a ticket about config. |
| `client-sites` | A paying client's own site or data, in a project you list under `clientProjects`. |
| `releases` | A release to users: an app store or Play Console release, a version publish, or a change to `eas.json` or `fastlane/`. |

Migrations are sorted by the SQL in the changed files. Payments, auth, client sites and releases go through a word and path check first, then the classifier set in `safety.classifier` decides.

## What always waits

These wait for you whatever the preset and the rules say:

- Running a migration that changes existing data. The deploy that would run it waits for its own tap.
- A ticket an agent filed from outside input, such as an email or a Claude MCP call.
- The first merge on a fresh install. `dobby init` pauses merges until you run `dobby resume merges`.

<!-- manual/doctor.md -->
# Doctor checks

> Every row dobby doctor prints, when it fails and the fix, plus the repo access rows dobby init reads.

`dobby doctor` exits with code 1 if any required check fails. `dobby doctor --json` prints every row as data. Rows marked optional never fail the exit code.

## Setup checks

| Row | Fails when | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Node | Node is older than 24. The `dobby` command also says so before it starts. | `brew install node`, or `fnm install 24` (no admin rights needed, Linux too). |
| shell | Neither zsh nor bash is installed. Project commands then run without a login shell. Optional. | Install zsh or bash. |
| git | git is missing. | `xcode-select --install` on macOS, `sudo apt install git` or `sudo dnf install git` on Linux. |
| git identity | git has no `user.email`, so builders cannot commit. | `git config --global user.email "<your GitHub email>"` |
| GitHub CLI | `gh` is missing. | `brew install gh` on macOS, the steps at cli.github.com on Linux. |
| GitHub sign-in | `gh` is not signed in. When GitHub cannot be reached, the row says so instead. | `gh auth login --web`, or check your connection. |
| git push over HTTPS | git has no GitHub sign-in, so pushes to `https://` remotes fail. Happens when `gh auth login` ran without a terminal. Fine if your remotes use SSH. Optional. | `gh auth setup-git` |
| GitHub token scopes | The token lacks `workflow` (pushes that touch workflow files) or `project` (the board). Optional. Not shown for fine-grained tokens. | `gh auth refresh -s workflow,project` |
| Claude Code | `claude` is missing. | `npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code` |
| Claude sign-in | Claude Code is not signed in (plan mode), or too old to have `claude auth status`. | Run `claude`, then `/login`, or `claude update`. |
| API key | API key mode is set but there is no `DOBBY_API_KEY`, or the key fails a small real call. With no network the row stays green and says it was not checked. | Add the key to `~/.config/dobby/secrets.env`. See [Cap spend](cap-spend.md#run-on-an-api-key). |
| config | There is no config file yet. | `dobby init` |
| config warnings | A config key is unknown or has a bad value. The row names it and suggests the key you probably meant. | `dobby config path`, then edit that file. |
| graphify | Not installed. Optional: builders and reviews get code maps from it. | `uv tool install graphifyy`, or `pipx install graphifyy`. |
| disk | Under 15 GB free where Dobby keeps its data. Optional. | Free up space. |
| Dobby | Never fails. Shows the installed version. | `npm i -g dobby-ai@latest && dobby jobs install` |
| time zone | `timezone` in the config is not this machine's zone. Optional. | `dobby config set timezone <zone>` |
| data folder | The data folder is on NFS or SMB. SQLite needs a local disk. Optional. | Set `DOBBY_DIR` to a local folder, then `dobby jobs install`. |
| Discord | No bot token. Optional. | `dobby init` and choose Discord, or add `DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN` to the secrets file and run `dobby discord setup`. |
| Jev | No key. Optional: a cheaper way to pick the review model. | Add `JEV_API_KEY` to the secrets file. |
| sandbox runner | The program that sandboxes builders was not found next to Dobby. Optional: builders then get only the credential scrub. | `npm i -g dobby-ai` |
| sandbox | On Linux, bubblewrap or socat is missing, or AppArmor blocks bubblewrap. On native Windows there is no sandbox. Optional: builders then get only the credential scrub. | The row prints the install or `sysctl` command. See [Install on Linux or WSL2](install-linux.md#install-the-sandbox). |
| background jobs | A job is not loaded, its last run exited with an error, a job from an older install is still loaded, or the jobs run another copy of Dobby (a temporary `npx` copy is named in the row). | `dobby jobs install` |

## Pipeline checks

After the setup checks, `dobby doctor` prints one row per pipeline check. With no projects yet, the rows say "no projects yet".

| Row | Fails when | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| stuck tickets | A ticket has been `running` for over 2 hours. | `dobby show <id>`, then `dobby retry <id>` or `dobby cancel <id>`. |
| origin/base | A project's `origin/<base>` branch does not resolve in its clone. | `git fetch` in the repo, or fix `base` in its project file. |
| claude session | Claude Code is signed out or did not answer in 60 seconds. | Run `claude`, then `/login`. |
| tick lock | The tick lock is held by a process that no longer exists, or has had no heartbeat for 90 minutes. A live tick shows as ok with its age. | Nothing: the next tick, `dobby run` or `dobby retry` clears a stale lock and puts the cut-off ticket back in the queue. |
| old pauses | A pause is over 7 days old. | `dobby pause status`, then `dobby resume <target>`. |
| review scan | No review scan ran for 2 hours. It runs every 15 minutes inside the `listener` job, or the `tick` job when Discord is off. | `dobby jobs status`. |
| stuck | A running or waiting ticket has not moved for over 24 hours. | `dobby show <id>`. |
| reviews | Reviews have been skipped for over 2 hours because of the budget. | Wait for the window, or raise `reviewCap`. |
| cap | Ready tickets have been held by the budget cap for over 3 hours. | Wait for the reset, or raise `pacing.weekCap`. |

## Repo access, read by `dobby init`

For each repo you pick, setup reads what Dobby's pull requests need. It only reads, and changes nothing on GitHub.

| Row | Meaning | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| GitHub access | This account cannot push to the repo (read-only, or the wrong account is active). Setup leaves the repo out. An SSO block shows the page that authorizes the token. | `gh auth switch`, or ask for write access. |
| Review rules | The base branch needs an approving or code-owner review. GitHub does not let you approve your own pull request, so Dobby's pull requests will wait for a second reviewer. | Add a reviewer who is not you, or loosen the rule. |
| Merge method | The repo has turned off the merge method Dobby uses. Setup sets `github.mergeMethod` to one that is on, when you have not set it yourself. | Set `github.mergeMethod`. |
| Signed commits | Signed commits are required and `github.mergeMethod` is `rebase`. GitHub does not sign rebase merges. | Use `squash` or `merge`. |
| Merge queue | Merges go through GitHub's merge queue. Dobby waits up to 30 minutes for the pull request to show as merged. | Nothing to fix. |

Before each build, Dobby also checks the `gh` sign-in, the remote and push access, and blocks the ticket with the reason instead of building and failing at the push. Set `"shipPreflight": false` to turn this off.

<!-- manual/pr-commands.md -->
# PR comment commands

> Every @dobby command you can write in a pull request comment, and its limits.

Commands are read by the review scan, every 15 minutes. Only users with write or admin access can give them. Comments from anyone else are ignored and cost nothing.

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `@dobby review` | Reviews the commits since the last review. Works on drafts. |
| `@dobby full review` | Reviews the whole pull request again. 3 per pull request per day. |
| `@dobby summary` | Rewrites the summary and risk line. |
| `@dobby describe` | Suggests a title and description. |
| `@dobby ask <question>` | A read-only answer about the pull request or the line the thread is on. |
| `@dobby learn` | In a reviewer thread: marks that finding as intentional for later reviews of this repo. |
| `@dobby resolve` | Resolves the reviewer's open threads. |
| `@dobby fix` | Queues a builder ticket for the open high and medium findings. Once per pull request per day. |
| `@dobby pause` | Stops automatic reviews on this pull request. |
| `@dobby resume` | Restarts automatic reviews on this pull request. |
| `@dobby quota` | Full reviews left today, and whether the plan allows work now. |
| `@dobby configuration` | The review settings in force for this repo. |
| `@dobby help` | This list. |

## Outside a comment

| Where | What it does |
|---|---|
| `@dobby ignore` in the pull request description | No automatic reviews of this pull request. |
| The `no-review` label (`review.skipLabel`) | No automatic reviews of this pull request. |
| 👎 on a reviewer comment, from someone with write access | Same as `@dobby learn`. |

## Limits

- On a public repo, commands stay off until you set `review.handle` or `review.botLogin`, because `dobby` may be someone's GitHub username.
- On a public repo, commands that run a model are refused on a pull request whose author is not you or a collaborator.
- `@dobby fix` needs `review.fix` on (the default). `@dobby learn` and 👎 need `review.learn` on (the default).

<!-- manual/stats.md -->
# Crash reports and usage stats

> Two optional switches, both off until you turn them on: what each one sends, every field, and how to turn them off.

Dobby asks two questions during `dobby init`: crash reports and usage stats. Pressing Enter answers no, `--yes` answers no, and no answer is off. They exist to show where installs stop in setup, what gets used and what breaks, without anything private leaving your machine.

## Turn them on or off

- `dobby stats` shows the status. `dobby stats on` or `dobby stats off` changes both; add `crashes` or `usage` to change one.
- `dobby stats show` prints exactly the usage payload the next daily send would carry.
- `dobby stats log` prints every payload that left this machine; the same lines are in `<data>/stats/sent.jsonl`.
- `dobby stats reset-id` makes a new random install id.
- The Settings page in the dashboard has the same two switches.
- Nothing is sent when `DO_NOT_TRACK` is set, when `DOBBY_STATS=off`, or when `CI` is set, whatever the switches say.
- Nothing is sent while `stats.endpoint` is empty.

## What is sent

Crash reports are sent when an unexpected error happens, at most 10 a day. An expected refusal (a typo in a command, a missing ticket) is not a crash. Usage stats are one batch a day at most, sent by the background tick job.

### every event

Added to every event below.

| Field | Values | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `install` | text | random id made when you said yes; `dobby stats reset-id` makes a new one |
| `v` | text | Dobby version |
| `os` | darwin \| linux | operating system |
| `node` | number | Node major version |
| `day` | text | UTC date, no time |

### setup_started

Sent: once, when `dobby init` starts (usage stats).

### setup_step

Sent: once per setup step (usage stats).

| Field | Values | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `props.step` | checks \| repos \| chat \| tools \| settings \| jobs \| first_ticket | which setup step |
| `props.ok` | true \| false | whether it passed |
| `props.reason` | gh_missing \| gh_signed_out \| claude_missing \| claude_signed_out \| git_missing \| node_old \| no_repos \| tests_failed \| skipped \| other | why it did not pass, from a fixed list |

### setup_done

Sent: once, when `dobby init` finishes (usage stats).

### first_ticket

Sent: once, the first time a ticket exists (usage stats).

### first_pr

Sent: once, the first time a ticket has a pull request (usage stats).

### first_merge

Sent: once, the first time a ticket has merged (usage stats).

### first_week_report

Sent: once, the first time the 7-day scoreboard or receipt was read (usage stats).

### setup_help

Sent: once, the first time you click Ask Claude in setup (usage stats).

| Field | Values | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `props.kind` | no-commands \| verify-failed \| check | what the help was asked about: a repo with no commands, a repo that failed to verify, or a failed machine check |
| `props.ok` | true \| false | whether Claude gave an answer that could be read |

### heartbeat

Sent: at most once a day (usage stats).

| Field | Values | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `props.plan` | pro \| max \| max20 \| api \| unknown | your Claude plan, from billing.planUsd (20 pro, 100 max, 200 max20) or api in API-key mode |
| `props.projects` | 0 \| 1 \| 2-3 \| 4+ | how many projects, as a range |
| `props.shipped` | 0 \| 1-2 \| 3-5 \| 6+ | tickets shipped in the last 24 hours, as a range |
| `props.sent_back` | 0 \| <25 \| 25-50 \| 50+ | share of pull requests the reviewer sent back in the last 7 days, in percent, as a range |
| `props.safety` | strict \| balanced \| autonomous | safety.preset |
| `props.review_auto` | off \| drafts \| on | review.auto |
| `props.merges_paused` | true \| false | whether merging is paused |
| `props.chat` | terminal \| discord | where Dobby asks you things |
| `props.week_cap` | number | pacing.weekCap, rounded down to a multiple of 10 |
| `props.week_used` | number | absent when no reading exists |
| `props.features` | object | which of these were used in the last 24 hours: dashboard, mcp_stdio, mcp_http, discord_buttons, brief_sent, deploy_tap, role_override, config_set |
| `props.roles` | object | runs per role in the last 24 hours, as a range; only roles that ran |

### crash

Sent: when Dobby fails with an unexpected error, at most 10 a day (crash reports).

| Field | Values | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `props.kind` | text | the error's class name, like TypeError |
| `props.where` | list of text | file:line of frames inside Dobby's own package, paths relative to the package; other frames are dropped |
| `props.command` | text | the dobby subcommand or job that failed |
| `props.code` | text | Dobby's own error code, if the error had one |

## Never sent

Repo or project names, paths, ticket or pull request titles or text, prompts, model output, code, URLs, GitHub or Discord usernames, emails, hostnames, tokens, error messages and exact times. The collector stores no IP address.

## The collector

It is a small Cloudflare Worker with a D1 database on the owner's own account (`stats-worker/` in the code folder). It checks every event against the same list as this page and refuses anything else. Rows older than 180 days are deleted every day.

<!-- manual/requirements.md -->
# Requirements

> The operating systems, tools, sign-ins and disk space Dobby needs.

- macOS or Linux
- Node 24 or newer
- GitHub CLI, signed in
- Claude Code on a Pro or Max plan, or an Anthropic API key

| Need | Details |
|---|---|
| Operating system | macOS, or Linux with systemd. Windows through WSL2 with systemd on. |
| Shell | zsh or bash. |
| git | With `user.email` set. |
| GitHub | Repos on github.com. GitLab, Bitbucket and GitHub Enterprise are not supported. |
| Claude | Claude Code only today. Other agent harnesses are coming. Bedrock and Vertex AI are not supported. |
| Linux sandbox | bubblewrap and socat. |
| Alpine and other musl systems | python3 and a C++ toolchain, to build the database driver. |
| Disk | 15 GB free on a local disk, not NFS or SMB. |
| Admin rights | Not needed. |

Optional: Discord for buttons and briefs, Tailscale for the dashboard on a phone, graphify for code maps.

:::note
Nothing runs while the computer sleeps.
:::

<!-- manual/data.md -->
# Where data lives

> Every folder and file Dobby writes on your machine, and the variables that move them.

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `~/.config/dobby/config.json` | Your settings. `dobby config path` prints where it is, and `dobby config show` prints the merged settings with secrets redacted. |
| `~/.config/dobby/secrets.env` | Tokens and keys, readable only by you. No command prints them. |
| `~/.config/dobby/projects/` | One project file per repo, with its knowledge and onboarding notes. |
| `~/.config/dobby/private-terms.txt` | Words that must never appear in text Dobby posts to a public repo. |
| `~/.local/share/dobby/` | The database (tickets, runs, pauses), worktrees and the receipt card. |
| `~/.local/share/dobby/logs/<job>.log` | One log per background job. Logs over 5 MB are cut to the last 1 MB once a day. |
| `~/.local/share/dobby/stats/sent.jsonl` | Every crash report or usage stat sent, if you turned them on. |
| `~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.dobby.*.plist` | The background jobs on macOS. |
| `~/.config/systemd/user/` | The background jobs on Linux. |
| `dobby.config.json` in Dobby's own install folder | Optional shared defaults. It can only make safety settings stricter. |

## Variables

| Variable | Effect |
|---|---|
| `DOBBY_DIR` | Moves the data folder. Use it when your home folder is on a network drive: SQLite's write-ahead log breaks on NFS and SMB. |
| `DOBBY_CONFIG` | Names the private config file. Its folder then holds the project files and secrets for that install. |

After you set or change either one, run `dobby jobs install` so the jobs use it.

## Settings order

Dobby reads its built-in defaults, then `dobby.config.json` in its install folder, then your private config file. A later layer wins, except that `dobby.config.json` can only tighten safety settings. All keys are in the [configuration reference](config.md).
